ns2:section.sectionText: 4 hr sect restricted to grads. Course surveys multidiciplinary issues of risk, safety, and reliability of nuclear power plants and other complex systems. Topics: technical and social risk-contribution factors and issues arising from their dynamic interactions; the advantages of integrating probabilistic and deterministic perspectives; probabilistic risk assessment and management; risk-informed decision-making for design, operation, and regulatory oversight; challenges of multi-dimensional risk evaluation considering diverse interrelated performance metirics (e.g. saftey, cost, quality) of high-risk organizations; issues of risk communication; public risk perceptions; and risk acceptance criteria. While the exammples will primarily focus on the nuclear power domain, the course will also cover current advancements in risk analysis of other socio-technical systems (e.g., space, oil and gas). Prerequisites: Jr or Sr or Graduate standing in Engineering.
